items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: not to work with but I worked on the same concert with Miles when Cannonball was there and Trane

ctx.x: Did you ever have occasion to work much with the Adderley brothers?

Not much but I have worked with them. One of my experiences, well I guess one of my main ways, not to work with but I worked on the same concert with Miles when Cannonball was there and Trane, and also when J.J. and Nat Adderley were together in the quintet. I was with Maynard and they were opening the concert with their band. And that was — but I’ve also recorded with Nat. I did a very bad CD with Nat too, I played very badly on that. It was very nice of him to give me the opportunity to do it. But I played some…
What was the name of that?

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Trane [John Coltrane] used to come to my house often, because his cousin Mary, that he wrote the song for, lived there.

ctx.x: What years are we talking about?

That was maybe the ’60s. Eric Dolphy lived there, and Freddie Hubbard, and Wayne Shorter. Wes [Montgomery] even stayed there for a while, and Joe Zawinul. Trane [John Coltrane] used to come to my house often, because his cousin Mary, that he wrote the song for, lived there. She was married to a trombone player.
